title: Integration and Access Ops Sync
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on networking/access gating, initial latency benchmark clarification, and next steps for SSO and firewall rules. Discussed small regression in p95 for long prompts and a workaround with prefix caching; agreed to schedule lab tests for on-prem routing and to share updated perf spreadsheet and SSO runbook.

HarborPay to provide firewall egress/IP list and test VPC route (by Fri 2026-09-19)

header: Meeting header: 2026-09-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Maya Singh, Jordan Li - Redwood; Ben Iglesias, Priya Nair, Sam Ortega, Lina Park - HarborPay
auto_sections: Summary: Quick recap above. Topics covered: access, latency, caching, SSO/KMS, next steps. Action items listed. Questions at end.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Ben - HarborPay: Ben here, Priya, Sam and Lina on our side.
[00:00:10] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Maya on the SE side, gonna walk through the perf notes.
[00:00:18] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan as well, I'll handle the access stuff.
[00:00:25] Priya - HarborPay: Great, let's dive. We're mostly looking to close the network gating and validate the p95 regression you flagged.
[00:00:34] Alex: Perfect. Quick agenda: access status, bench results recap (yesterday's run), prefix/KV cache ideas, SSO/KMS checklist, and next steps.
[00:00:45] Ben: On access - we added the initial keys to staging but the gateway is dropping connections occasionally; we think it's the firewall.
[00:00:52] Jordan: Ok, can you confirm the egress rules? We published the IP ranges in the doc, but sometimes cloud NATs rewrite addresses.
[00:00:59] Ben: We'll grab the exact NAT IPs and share.
[00:01:05] Maya: On the bench - we re-ran the synthetic load with the same prompts. p50 looked fine ~120ms but p95 moved to ~420ms for long prompts with 2k tokens, which is higher than the earlier run.
[00:01:18] Sam: Is that with kv cache enabled?
[00:01:21] Maya: There was a partial kv cache hit rate, maybe around 60% due to prompt variability. We suspect cache fragmentation and batching alignment.
[00:01:32] Priya: Any config change on your side overnight?
[00:01:35] Maya: We updated a kernel selection tweak for the quant path, might have impacted tail latency for long sequences.
[00:01:42] Alex: There's a possibility the kernel change improved throughput but worsened p95 for >1.5k tokens; we can revert and test.
[00:01:49] Ben: For our use, p95 is more important than peak throughput.
[00:01:52] Jordan: Noted. We'll prioritize a rollback candidate and also propose a prefix-caching tweak.
[00:02:00] Lina - HarborPay: On SSO, we're ready to start SAML config but need the metadata and an assertion example.
[00:02:06] Alex: We'll send the SAML metadata and a sample SSO assertion. Also include recommended session TTL and SCIM mapping notes.
[00:02:13] Priya: Good. Also, SOC two scope: do you capture audit logs for model access? I think you mentioned audit trails earlier.
[00:02:20] Maya: Yes, we produce audit logs with token-level events and model id, but the retention in this pilot is by default 7 days; enterprise retention options available.
[00:02:30] Priya: 7 days might be too short for us, we'll need 90 days for the audit review.
[00:02:33] Alex: We'll surface enterprise retention plan in the security pack; Maya will follow up.
[00:02:40] Sam: Back to perf - can you share the query distribution? We're curious if a few outliers caused the p95 spike.
[00:02:47] Maya: Yes, we'll attach the token distribution CSV. Early look: 85% of requests are <800 tokens, about 10% in 800-1500, and 5% over 1500; the tail is driven by the 5%.
[00:02:59] Ben: So perhaps we can route long requests to a different config? Maybe dedicated flame? (laughs)
[00:03:05] Alex: We can route long sequences to a higher-memory variant or a quant-profile that favours latency over cost. We also have auto-fallback policies.
[00:03:13] Priya: Will that change the response semantics? We can't risk differences in completions for finance flows.
[00:03:18] Maya: Good point. We can A/B the variant and run a gold prompt set to check regressions. If semantics diverge, we won't switch.
[00:03:25] Sam: Ok. Also, what about kv cache warmup? Is there a way to preload common prefixes?
[00:03:30] Maya: Yes — we can seed prefix cache with your common customer templates. We'll provide a script to prepopulate. That should cut tail latency for repeat patterns.
[00:03:37] Ben: We'll provide the top 20 templates.
[00:03:40] Jordan: On the gateway issue, one more ask: can HarborPay temporarily open a test route to Redwood's staging IPs so we can reproduce the drop?
[00:03:46] Ben: Yes we can. We'll open to the staging block and send confirmation.
[00:03:50] Priya: Also need to check KMS integration — our key rotations are monthly, we need deterministic envelopes and HSM compatibility.
[00:03:57] Alex: We support external KMS via customer-managed keys, and HSM-backed stores. We'll share the KMS integration spec.
[00:04:04] Lina: Any blockers for on-prem proxying? We're testing an air-gapped-ish env for regulated flows.
[00:04:10] Maya: On-prem routing needs an agent and the private control plane; we've done similar setups. For the POC, we recommend a thin proxy forwarding to a dedicated pool. We'll schedule a design session.
[00:04:19] Ben: Sounds good. Timeline wise, we want to validate routing and SSO before the next executive review on Oct 1.
[00:04:27] Alex: Ok that's reasonable. We'll deliver the docs and bench updates within the week.
[00:04:33] -- (brief silence; typing) --
[00:10:12] Maya: I uploaded the initial raw bench logs to the shared drive, note there are some labels mis-encoded, you'll see tokens counted as characters in a couple places — sorry about that, we'll re-export.
[00:10:22] Sam: No problem, we can still eyeball the distribution.
[00:10:27] Ben: One question - do you have a recommended autoscale policy for our peak windows? We have bursty payroll runs.
[00:10:34] Jordan: For bursting we recommend reserved baseline plus short-lived burst capacity; set autoscale to add x N GPU nodes when queue depth crosses threshold for 30s, and keep a short cool-down. We can share a recommended config.
[00:10:45] Priya: Any cost ballpark for that? We need to justify to finance.
[00:10:49] Alex: We'll prepare a cost delta sheet comparing reserved-only vs reserved+burst. That's part of the deliverables.
[00:10:55] Ben: Back to the p95 - will reverting the kernel change be risky?
[00:11:00] Maya: Minimal risk; we can test the rollback in a canary and monitor error rates and output diffs.
[00:11:06] Sam: Can we run a 2-hour smoke with our top 100 prompts?
[00:11:09] Maya: Yes, we'll schedule that once we have the pre-seeded cache and your firewall rule open.
[00:11:15] Alex: Action items captured. Any other security concerns?
[00:11:19] Priya: Make sure SAML assertions include roles mapping; we need RBAC on console access.
[00:11:24] Jordan: We'll include SCIM and role mapping examples.
[00:11:28] Lina: For the audit trail, will the logs include request bodies or just metadata?
[00:11:33] Maya: By default metadata; request bodies are redacted unless you opt-in for longer retention and special handling. We can propose an approver flow.
[00:11:41] Priya: Ok please draft that flow.
[00:11:44] -- crosstalk --
[00:20:05] Alex: Quick recap: Redwood will send SAML metadata, perf CSV, KV seed script, and cost delta sheet. HarborPay to provide firewall list, top templates, and roster for SCIM. We'll schedule an on-prem design session and a canary rollback bench.
[00:20:18] Ben: Confirmed. We'll try to get the egress list by Friday.
[00:20:23] Sam: One more tiny item — we saw occasional 503s during heavy batch sims, can you check queue backpressure in the logs?
[00:20:29] Maya: We'll surface queue metrics and an annotated trace for the 503 windows.
[00:20:33] Priya: Also ping the compliance contact about SOC two scope.
[00:20:37] Alex: Will do.
[00:20:41] Jordan: I'll open a scheduling poll for the design/bench sessions.
[00:20:45] Lina: Thanks everyone.
[00:20:48] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet. Meeting adjourned.
questions: What caused the p95 spike for long prompts?
Can Redwood support 90-day audit log retention for the pilot?
Will prefix cache seeding materially reduce tail latency for our templates?
